body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 6 models with a format search (of 279 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 24.7 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.8 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 4 of 6 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 66%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's), facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 67%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and openai-community/gpt2 (perplexity 43.3 → 48.4, higher is worse).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB), groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB), add output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 36.2 dB) and linear bias in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 36.5 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): mul outputs end furthest from full precision, facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 keeping only -0.8 dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), linear in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 7.6 dB), attention in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), silu in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 10.5 dB), attention in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.1 dB), linear in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 11.3 dB), add in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 11.3 dB), layernorm in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.5 dB) and gelu_tanh in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 11.6 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 3254 (71%), fp8_e1m6 873 (19%), fp8_e3m4 447 (9.72%), ufp8_e2m6 23 (0.50%), ufp8_e3m5 1 (0.02%); 0.52% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where an output's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.4 dB) and upsample in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.9 dB).

1 missing capability keep 29 operations in 1 model (of 5 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (29 operations in 1 model). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 29 operations in 1 model: 29 calls (1.22% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256. Cost today: 0 of 29 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 29 wait for one; 0 workarounds proposed, 0 passing its check, none evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 405 of 707 tensors passed between kernels (57%) in 5 models: 243 for attention heads split or merged, 142 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 255 operations (255 calls, 11% of all calls; 99.3 G MACs, 4.21% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → add (other reshapes) 58 and linear → mul (other reshapes) 56; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and google/vit-base-patch16-224 (36).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 405 of 707 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 705 operations in 5 models (705 calls, 30% of all calls), most often silu (210), layernorm (151) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst 9.2 dB SQNR over 705 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 43, most 81 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 81 planned groups), over 5 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 34.4 powers of ten for mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (largest value 1.48e+04).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 705 operations limited by the LUT and up to 81 kernel launches per pass

body:
**IPU architecture costs, most costly first (per the survey):**

1. **Compute efficiency — unknown.** No kernel has been measured, so MAC utilisation is not yet known; this is the biggest open question rather than a measured cost.

2. **Quantisation accuracy (NX8 formats).** Across 6 models with a format search, model outputs lose a median 23.6 dB SQNR vs full precision, worst 12.8 dB (SD v1.5 VAE); 4 of 6 models lose prediction quality (worst: GPT-2 perplexity 43.3 → 71.2; DiT and SD-VAE token agreement drop to ~67%). The most fragile tensors are layernorm, add, mul and linear outputs in DiT-XL-2-256 and SD v1.5 (32–37 dB in their best formats), and mul output in DiT keeps only −0.8 dB along the data path. A wider format or per-row choice at a handful of sites (silu, conv2d, upsample in SD-VAE) would recover most of it.

3. **Layout conversions.** 369 of 659 inter-kernel tensors (56%) in 4 models must be rearranged by the reading kernel — 207 for attention head split/merge — affecting 231 calls (11% of calls) holding 4.2% of MACs; extra cycles are not yet measured.

4. **Resource limits (LUT + launches).** 656 operations (30% of calls) run through the 256-entry LUT (silu, layernorm, groupnorm most), with worst 9.2 dB SQNR; up to 81 kernel launches per forward pass; 13 outputs sit at the FP32 limit. IMEM use is unmeasured.

5. **Missing instructions.** Only one gap: run-time addressing, blocking 29 calls (1.3% of calls, no MACs) in DiT — all awaiting a workaround, with 0 extra kernels so far; adding it would put those 29 calls directly on chip.
